content.text: {"primary_meaning":"Divine judgment or wrath arriving as overwhelming calamity. In prophetic and apocalyptic imagery, a storm or tempest commonly portrays God’s forceful visitation against sin, nations, or false security.","primary_basis":["Isaiah 28:2—an overpowering storm depicts the Lord’s judgment.","Isaiah 29:6—thunder, earthquake, whirlwind, and tempest accompany divine punishment.","Jeremiah 23:19-20; 30:23-24—the storm of the LORD is explicitly identified with his wrath and judgment.","Ezekiel 13:11-13—a storm, flooding rain, and hail express God’s wrath against false prophets.","Nahum 1:3-6—the whirlwind and storm portray the LORD’s power and anger in judgment.","Psalm 83:13-15—a tempest and hurricane are invoked as images of God pursuing his enemies.","Proverbs 1:27—calamity and distress arrive like a storm as the consequence of rejecting wisdom."],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"Trials, suffering, fear, or instability in human life, through which faith is tested and divine deliverance may be experienced.","basis":["Matthew 8:23-27; Mark 4:35-41; Luke 8:22-25—the calming of the storm is frequently applied in Christian teaching to fear and trials.","Matthew 7:24-27—the storm tests whether a life is founded on Christ’s teaching.","Psalm 107:23-30—sailors in a storm cry to God, who brings them to safety.","Jonah 1:4-16—a storm creates crisis, exposes disobedience, and leads to repentance."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Chaos, disorder, or hostile powers threatening creation and God’s people.","basis":["Genesis 1:2 is often read alongside broader biblical imagery of unruly waters, though it does not itself mention a storm.","Psalm 46:1-3; 69:1-2,14-15—turbulent waters represent danger and overwhelming chaos.","Psalm 107:25-29—God exercises sovereignty over stormy seas.","Mark 4:35-41 is sometimes interpreted as Christ’s victory over chaotic or demonic powers, not merely bad weather."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"A manifestation of God’s presence, majesty, and sovereign power—a storm theophany rather than primarily a symbol of punishment.","basis":["Psalm 18:7-15—the LORD appears amid clouds, thunder, hail, and wind.","Psalm 29—the divine voice rules over thunder, waters, and the storm.","Job 38:1; 40:6—God answers Job from the whirlwind.","Ezekiel 1:4-28—a storm wind and great cloud introduce the vision of divine glory.","Nahum 1:3—the storm is associated with God’s majestic passage."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"The church or the believer endangered by persecution, with the boat or ark representing God’s people and Christ preserving them.","basis":["Matthew 8:23-27 and Mark 4:35-41 received ecclesial readings in patristic and later Christian interpretation.","Genesis 6–9 and 1 Peter 3:20-21 contribute to related ark-and-church symbolism, although the storm itself is not consistently isolated as the symbol of persecution."],"prominence":"minority"}],"has_settled_consensus":false,"confidence":"medium","notes":"There is no single settled symbolic meaning applicable to every biblical storm. Prophetic references most characteristically use storm imagery for divine judgment, while preaching and devotional interpretation often treats storms as life’s trials. Narrative, poetic, and theophanic contexts can instead emphasize chaos, deliverance, or God’s presence and power."}
